tier_reason: Upgraded from C: Sputnik's own evidence is the peer-reviewed SC'20 paper (Gale, Zaharia, Young, Elsen, 'Sparse GPU Kernels for Deep Learning', arXiv 2006.10901, cited by the repo and by google-research/sgk), which a search-result snippet reports as a 3.58x geometric-mean SpMM speedup over cuSPARSE on a V100 (paper host egress-blocked here, not opened). The third-party Torch-Sputnik A100 table alone would be C (no CUDA version, flags, units or method).

corrections.claimed_speedup: Torch-Sputnik README (A100, third-party PyTorch binding; the tables give no time unit, values consistent with ms): M=N=K=4096 Sputnik 2.52 vs cuSPARSE 10.97 at density 0.05 (about 4.4x, derived from page data), 4.02 vs 21.68 at 0.1 (5.4x), 13.05 vs 107.38 at 0.5 (8.2x); M=N=K=64 Sputnik 0.0045 to 0.0075 vs cuSPARSE 0.086 to 0.147. SC'20 paper (per search snippet, not opened): 3.58x geometric-mean SpMM speedup over cuSPARSE on V100 across the Deep Learning Matrix Collection.
corrections.caveats: The A100 numbers come from a 4-star third-party PyTorch binding repo whose tables state no time unit, CUDA version, host CPU or timing method; Sputnik's own README has no numbers. The SC'20 paper (peer reviewed) is the primary evidence but could not be opened here (arxiv.org and the Berkeley PDF host are egress-blocked); its 3.58x V100 geometric mean is from a search snippet. The Torch-Sputnik table shows dense cuBLAS at 7.29 for 4096^3, so Sputnik is slower than dense at density 0.5 (13.05) and 0.25 (7.87) and wins only at density 0.2 and below. Repository archived 2026-04-19; last commit 2020-11-04 (19 commits).

notes: Torch-Sputnik numbers match the record, but the record's '(page states ms)' is wrong: the tables give no unit (the cuBLAS 4096^3 figure is plausible as ms on an A100). Metadata confirmed: Apache-2.0, 289 stars, archived 2026-04-19, last commit 2020-11-04, so abandoned.

tier_reason: README 'Performance at a Glance' table matches the quoted times and speedups; the generator (generate_benchmark_report.py calling tests/benchmark_large_scale.py) is public, but no CPU, compiler, flags or thread/process count is given, so first-party C.

corrections.workload: Variable-block sparse matrix operations on random block-sparse matrices (README table of 500 to 20,000 blocks, about 9,000 to 360,000 rows; the repo's report script defaults to block sizes 16-20 and about 200 neighbour blocks per row), VBCSR versus SciPy CSR; the README does not say which operation (SpMV, sparse-dense or SpMM) the table times, nor the thread or MPI process count.

notes: Numbers verified (4.21x at 500 blocks, 0.0049 s vs 0.0209 s, up to 4.49x at 20,000 blocks, 0.1866 s vs 0.8377 s). The record's 'serial run' is not stated on the page, so I removed it. The current report script defaults (500/1000/2000 SpMV blocks) do not reproduce the README's 20,000-block range, so the table predates it. Metadata confirmed: AGPL-3.0, 1 star, not a fork, 211 commits, last commit 2026-09-28; README clone URL is the placeholder github.com/yourusername/vbcsr.
